newsitem.title: UK: UK pension funds moving to money purchase schemes.
newsitem.headline: UK pension funds moving to money purchase schemes.

text.p: UK pension funds have signalled they expect to move decisively away from traditional final salary pension schemes towards money purchase pensions in the next two years, a survey from Flemings shows.

The poll was carried out for Fleming Investment Management among more than 100 leading finance directors and pension fund managers in industry, commerce and the public sector responsible for pension funds totalling an estimated 20 billion stg.
Only 24 percent of the pensions managers surveyed had money purchase schemes now but 74 percent expect to be offering them in two years time, Fleming said.

While traditional salary pension schemes are calculated from the level of the contributor's final salary on retirement. Money purchase schemes, on the other hand, base payouts on what the individual contributes through the life of the policy.

Kenneth Inglis, chairman of Fleming Investment Management told a conference on money purchase schemes last week he expects UK money purchase assets to top 50 billion stg in the next 10 years, providing pensions for at least one million people.
